findings.summary: Output matching passed. NACA took 9.60 s; OCR was 78.7%. Page-assigned recognition left GPU 3 idle.
observations: The ordinary NACA call took 9.60 s: OCR 7.55 s (78.7%), embedding 1.91 s (19.9%). One warm-up and the extra instrumented call are excluded.
Mean GPU busy during OCR on GPUs 0–3: 42.9%, 51.7%, 95.0%, 0.0%. Mean power: 50.9 W, 57.4 W, 70.5 W, 27.7 W.
One-second sampling produced only 7 OCR-window samples per GPU. Busy percentages measure sampled activity, not percentage of peak arithmetic throughput or memory bandwidth.
Page-assigned recognition leaves GPU 3 without OCR work for the three-page PDF. The longer page determines completion; the other page workers finish earlier.
Batch invariance is enabled. The full instrumented output passed exact OCR/chunk matching and embedding checks against the shared vLLM references. All 71 NACA regions ended with EOS.
The bounded traces cover 32 engine iterations per active recognizer. An iteration can include several regions and different vision/prefill/decode work. Raw kernel counts are not normalized per token.
Hardware counters for achieved compute throughput, DRAM bandwidth and occupancy were not collected.
findings.next_step: The completed all-GPU variant reduced ordinary NACA OCR to 3.34 s while preserving the shared reference outputs.
findings.optimization: The all-GPU experiment is complete. Its profile points next to fp32 embedding, which now accounts for 35.4% of total latency.

hardware_counters.scope: Activity, power, scheduler samples and bounded traces do not measure percentage of peak compute or bandwidth
